bib.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling" (AutoTTS). Tong Zheng (first author), Haolin Liu, Chengsong Huang and others (UMD, UVA, WUSTL, UNC, Google, Meta). Preprint, arXiv:2605.08083v2, cs.CL, 12 May 2026. First-author month/year: May 2026. No venue.

COVERAGE: I read the extractable text of all 25 pages, which is about 86.5k chars. That includes the body, the Limitation and Broader Impact sections (Appendices A and B), the discovery prompt (Appendix C) and the discovered controller (Appendix D). I read only part of the Appendix C prompt and part of the Appendix D code, and I skimmed the references. I did not run figure captions and did not view the figures. Figure notes below come from the extracted caption text.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: An explorer LLM agent (Claude Code) can design a test-time-scaling (TTS) controller by editing code. It scores each candidate against an offline replay of pre-collected trajectories, so no base-LLM calls are needed during search.
  number: $39.9 and 160 minutes for the whole discovery, over 5 rounds.
  setup: Replay matrix of 128 trajectories per (model, problem) at temperature 0.7 with a 500-token probe interval. Four Qwen3 models (0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B). The search set is AIME24.
  quote: "the five-round discovery process costs only $39.9 and takes 160 minutes"
  where: p.8, section 5.5

- Claim: The discovered controller beats the handcrafted baselines on held-out benchmarks in 3 of 4 models. At β=0.5 it matches self-consistency (SC@64) accuracy with much fewer tokens.
  number: about 69.5% fewer tokens; 45.3 vs 45.2 average accuracy.
  setup: Held-out AIME25 and HMMT25. The controller was optimized on AIME24 only. Baselines are SC@64, ASC, ESC and Parallel-Probe.
  quote: "it reduces token consumption by approximately 69.5% compared to SC@64 while maintaining on-par accuracy on average across all four models (45.3 vs. 45.2)"
  where: p.5, section 5.1
  Caveat: Qwen3-8B is only competitive ("62.7 vs. 62.8 for SC@64"). On Qwen3-4B the held-out average is 60.5 for β=1.0 against 60.4 for Parallel-Probe and 60.2 for ASC, so the margin is within noise. ASC uses fewer tokens there (333.1k vs 648.6k). AIME24 is the search set, so its numbers are not held-out.

- Claim: Forcing the agent to expose a single monotone hyperparameter β, with every other hyperparameter derived from it, stops the search overfitting the search set.
  number: Without β, held-out accuracy falls from 53.1 to 49.0 and tokens drop from 575.5K to 93.3K.
  setup: Table 3, averaged over four models. Agents otherwise proposed up to 10 hyperparameters in only 5 rounds.
  quote: "resulting in a drastic token reduction (575.5K to 93.3K) accompanied by an accuracy drop from 53.1 to 49.0 on held-out benchmarks"
  where: p.7-8, section 5.4 and Table 3
  Note: the failure was collapse onto aggressive pruning thresholds. The no-β variant also cost more to search ($46.4 vs $39.9).

- Claim: Feeding the explorer full execution traces, not only scalar accuracy and cost, gives a better controller.
  number: Without traces, held-out accuracy is 51.6 vs 53.1 and tokens are 824.3K vs 575.5K. Search cost is $30.9 vs $39.9.
  setup: Same as the ablation above.
  quote: "Without this, the discovered controller achieves worse performance while allocating much more tokens."
  where: p.8, section 5.4
  Note: the paper credits Meta-Harness [20] for the finding that detailed execution feedback helps discovery.

- Claim: The discovered controller transfers to another model family and to a non-math task.
  number: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on HMMT25: 27.2 accuracy at 533.9K tokens, vs 26.7 at 985.7K for SC@64. Qwen3-1.7B on GPQA-Diamond: 41.6 at 151.0K tokens (β=0.5), vs 41.3 at 510.0K for SC@64.
  setup: Table 2. Each of these is one model and one benchmark, with no repeated seeds reported.
  quote: "the β= 0.5 variant reduces the token cost from 510.0K to 151.0K"
  where: p.6-7, section 5.3

- Claim: The discovery trajectory shows the agent correcting itself. Round 1 over-optimizes for tokens and accuracy drops. Later rounds raise the budget to recover accuracy, then alternate between efficiency and accuracy steps.
  number: none
  setup: β=1, 5 rounds, AIME24 search set and AIME25+HMMT25 held-out.
  quote: "The initial controller is overly aggressive in reducing token usage, leading to relatively low accuracy."
  where: p.8, section 5.6 (Figure 4)

- Claim: The discovered controller (CMC, Confidence Momentum Controller) uses four mechanisms: an EMA-trend stopping gate, width and depth coupled through the EMA delta, extra probe steps for branches that agree with the pool winner, and abandoning a branch only after persistent deviation.
  number: none
  setup: Appendix D code listing.
  quote: "CMC replaces ALL instantaneous gates with a single EMA momentum gate"
  where: Appendix D, p.17-18
  Note: "difficult to arrive at through manual intuition alone" is the authors' assertion and is not tested.

- Claim: The authors' stance is that human effort belongs in designing the environment (states, actions, feedback, objective), not in designing strategies.
  number: none
  quote: "the right place to invest human effort is in environment design, not strategy design"
  where: p.3, introduction

LIMITS
- The authors concede two limits. The environment covers only width-depth control. The search relies on a frontier coding agent (Claude Code), and they leave open whether open-source agents can match it (Appendix A).
- The search has one dataset (AIME24), 5 rounds, and one run. The paper reports no seeds, variance or confidence intervals for the discovery itself.
- The held-out benchmarks are also math (AIME25, HMMT25), from the same family as the search set. Only two out-of-distribution checks exist, in Table 2.
- Replay is valid only because the action space is limited to reading pre-collected trajectories. Strategies that need fresh generation are out of scope.
- The selection rule picks the best accuracy on the search set, not the best trade-off.
- Some held-out averages favour baselines. Examples are the 4B and 8B rows, and ASC's lower token use on 4B.
- The model scales are small (0.6B to 8B).

BUILDS ON
- Parallel-Probe [6]: the data-collection protocol and a baseline.
- Meta-Harness [20]: exposing full execution histories to the proposer.
- Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2022), ASC (Aggarwal et al. 2023), ESC (Li et al. 2024).
- FunSearch, EoH, AlphaEvolve and ADAS for LLM-driven program search.
- TTT-Discover and ThetaEvolve.

CODE
- Appendix C contains the discovery prompt. Its key rules are: expose only `beta`, make the map monotone in `beta`, and do not peek at gold answers or held-out splits. The history lives in `code_base/history/rNNNN_<timestamp>_<uid>/`, with a `method.py` snapshot and per-question trace JSONL for each round (p.15-16).
- Appendix D contains the `OptimalController` class (p.17-18).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.1): the loop of construct environment, propose candidate, evaluate, store to history. This is the best single picture of the loop.
- Fig 2 (p.2): existing TTS methods drawn as paths through the width-depth space.
- Fig 3 (p.7): accuracy against tokens for four held-out settings.
- Fig 4 (p.8): per-round trajectory on the search set and held-out sets. It shows the agent overcorrecting and then recovering.
- Table 3 (p.7): the ablation. It is the compact evidence for the single-knob rule and for traces.

PLACEMENT (relative to notes in `ai-engineering/04-loop-engineering/notes/`)
- It is on topic, but only partly about self-improvement. The paper is a proposer loop (agent edits code, scorekeeper scores it, history is kept) in a narrow domain. The model weights are not changing.
- Best fit is `03-the-scorekeeper.md`. The paper's real lesson is that a deterministic, cheap, replayable scorer is what makes a loop affordable ($39.9 vs repeated LLM calls). A richer trace beats a scalar score ("Without Execution Traces" row).
- Second fit is `09-failure-modes-and-guardrails.md`. Overfitting the search set is the failure mode. The single-knob monotone constraint is the guardrail. The aggressive first round that gets corrected is a behaviour worth citing.
- I would not add it to `08-self-improving-loops.md`, which is over length. At most, put a one-line cross-reference there that points to 03.
- I did not open the notes, so I cannot say whether 08 already cites Meta-Harness.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction was clean, with only minor garbling in tables (bold markers run into numbers). The Table 1 cells I quoted were read as printed.
- No embedded instructions were found. The Appendix C prompt is the paper's own content and I did not act on it.
- Figure captions were not extracted via `figures.py`, and the figures themselves were not viewed.
